title: RBI Policy Rates
plainSummary: The RBI's repo rate stands at 5.25%, with CRR at 3%. These set the cost of money across the economy — your loan EMIs, deposit returns and how much cash banks must keep aside all move with them.

metrics.label: Policy Repo Rate
metrics.plain: The rate at which the RBI lends to banks. Up = loans and EMIs get costlier.

metrics.label: Fixed Reverse Repo Rate
metrics.plain: The rate the RBI pays banks to park money with it, absorbing liquidity.

metrics.label: Standing Deposit Facility Rate
metrics.plain: The floor rate at which banks park spare cash with the RBI (no collateral).

metrics.label: Marginal Standing Facility Rate
metrics.plain: The emergency rate banks pay to borrow overnight from the RBI.

metrics.label: Bank Rate
metrics.plain: The rate the RBI charges on longer-term lending to banks; a policy signal.

metrics.label: CRR
metrics.plain: Share of deposits banks must keep as cash with the RBI, earning nothing.

metrics.label: SLR
metrics.plain: Share of deposits banks must hold in safe assets like government bonds.

metrics.label: INR / 1 USD
metrics.plain: How many rupees one US dollar buys right now (FBIL reference).

provenance.note: Scraped from the RBI homepage rates box; FX reference from FBIL.
